## How to apply the rule above — and its limit

The block above is right that this is Next.js 16 and your training data may be wrong about it. It is
**not** an instruction to read that doc tree before every edit: it is hundreds of files and
megabytes of prose, and the repo-root `CLAUDE.md` says **do not read `node_modules`**. Two rules in
contradiction are worse than either alone, so **this section is the resolution.**

**Read a Next.js doc when — and only when — you are about to use a framework API and are not certain
of its current signature or conventions**, or when something behaves differently from what you
expect. Real triggers here: route handlers, `generateMetadata`, `next/og`, caching and revalidation,
`params` / `useSearchParams` being async, `next/image` config and `remotePatterns`, middleware, and
anything crossing the server/client boundary.

**Do not read it for** ordinary React or TypeScript, a styling or copy change, a component that
touches no framework API, or anything already answered by `CLAUDE.md` / `COMPONENTS.md`.

**Find the one file; never browse the tree.** Glob or grep `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/` for
the API name and read only what matches — `index.md` is a welcome page, not a file index.

⚠️ **Reading docs here is the ONE sanctioned exception to the no-`node_modules` rule.** Never read
package source, and never import from a `node_modules` path.
